note: py_module/py_scope/py_binding emitted in frozen column order (24/25/29). Stage-2 entity models and enums also landed (py_type 25, py_type_base 16, py_method 36, py_method_parameter 22, py_import 24) but are NOT yet populated by an extractor.

subject: scopeOrdinal is evaluation order, not source order
detail: symtable orders a block's children by CONSTRUCTION order. Signature parts are evaluated before the body exists, so in `def __init__(self, spec=lambda: 1)` the lambda is a SIBLING built first: lambda=ordinal 0, method=ordinal 1, even though the def starts at an earlier column. Sorting children by (line,column) inverts them. Affected 260 scope rows across the stdlib sweep. Now mirrors symtable.c exactly: defaults, kw_defaults, annotations (posonly, args, vararg, kwarg, kwonly, returns), decorators, body.

subject: symtable visits try/else BEFORE except handlers
detail: CPython's symtable.c Try_kind visits body, then orelse, then handlers, then finalbody — not source order, and not the order the compiler uses. locale.py depends on it: its two conditional getpreferredencoding defs (lines 652 and 657) get ordinals 30 and 29 respectively.

subject: symtable.py decides module scope by NAME, not block type
detail: symtable.py does `module_scope = (self._table.name == "top")`, so ANY function or class literally named `top` receives module-scope semantics for is_local/is_global — a bound name reports both. Reproduced deliberately because symtable is the oracle. Real case: poplib.POP3.top reports its parameters as is_global=true. Flagging as a CPython wart the engine may want to know about rather than a parser choice.

subject: PEP 563 suppresses annotation visits entirely
detail: Under `from __future__ import annotations`, CPython 3.10 does not visit annotation expressions at all, so a TYPE_CHECKING-only import used solely in a signature is is_referenced=false. Without the future import the same name is is_referenced=true. Verified both directions. Consequence for the engine: is_referenced cannot be used to decide whether an import is live when futureImports contains `annotations`.

subject: tree-sitter parse ceiling confirmed at exactly 32767 characters
detail: Measured against tree-sitter 0.21.1 / tree-sitter-python 0.21.0: a 32,767-character buffer parses, 32,768 throws `Invalid argument`. Characters, not bytes — 29,007 chars of CJK (87,007 UTF-8 bytes) parses fine. PythonParser streams in 8KB chunks above 30,000 chars, mirroring java-parser.ts:43. Files are never split, so there is always exactly one root and module containment is intact.

subject: Python 2 three-tier detection verified against the grammar
detail: Tier 1 node types (print_statement, exec_statement, chevron) all parse with hasError=false, confirming rejection cannot rely on parse failure. Tier 2 shapes verified distinguishable: `except E, e:` has a direct comma child where `except E as e:` produces an as_pattern, and a Py2 tuple parameter is a tuple_pattern whose PARENT is `parameters`/`lambda_parameters` where the legal Py3 `(a,b) = x` has parent `assignment`. Tier 3 backticks confirmed indistinguishable in the tree (string/string_start/string_content/string_end, hasError=false), so a raw-source scan is required; the scan tracks string and comment state so backticks in docstrings and comments do not cause false rejections. 15/15 detector cases pass, including 9 negative Py3 cases.

subject: emissionRegime PY3_12_PLUS currently refuses rather than emits
detail: The extractor throws when emissionRegime != PY3_0_11. Rationale: the 3.12 regime differs structurally at every list/set/dict comprehension (PEP 709), the pinned oracle is 3.10.4 and refuses to run under any other interpreter, so emitting 3.12 facts would produce rows nothing can adjudicate. Refusing seemed better than guessing. Confirm that is the behaviour you want, or tell me to implement the subtractive gate unverified.
options: keep refusing until a 3.12 oracle exists
implement the gate now, marked unverified

subject: nonlocal with no binding in any enclosing scope
detail: `nonlocal x` where no enclosing scope binds x is a SyntaxError in CPython, so symtable never produces a fact set for such a file and the oracle cannot adjudicate it. The parser currently records the declared intent (a NONLOCAL binding with scope FREE and no target) rather than rejecting the file, on the grounds that rejecting loses every other fact in it. Escalating per brief: this is a question about what the reasoning engine needs, not a parser decision.

subject: star-import expansion remains unexpanded
detail: `from x import *` sets py_scope.usesWildcardImport and emits one py_import row with isWildcard=true, binding no names. The parser does not expand it even when the target module is in the repo and its __all__ is static. Per brief this is a your-call item: expanding would invent bindings symtable does not have (so the oracle would report them as spurious), while not expanding leaves a known soundness hole the engine must handle. 22 sites in the measured corpus.

subject: py_method_parameter.position ordering — parser vs oracle ast dump
detail: Gate 2 disagreement, resolved in the parser's favour with third-party evidence. For `def full_signature(a, b, /, c, d=10, *args, e, f=20, **kwargs)` the oracle's ast dump lists params grouped (posonlyargs, args, kwonlyargs, then vararg, then kwarg) giving a,b,c,d,e,f,args,kwargs; the parser emits canonical signature order a,b,c,d,args,e,f,kwargs. CPython's own inspect.signature reports the parser's order exactly. This matters rather than being cosmetic: positional argument flow indexes on `position`, so placing KEYWORD_ONLY params at indices 4-5 ahead of *args at 6 would let a rule bind a 5th positional argument to `e`, which can never receive one. All paramKind values agreed; only the sequence differed. Parser unchanged; the differential checker now compares parameters as a set of name:kind pairs. Flagging in case A0 wants the ast dump reordered so the two agree positionally.

subject: isGenerator — oracle's _has_yield walks into nested functions
detail: The oracle's ast-side helper `_has_yield` returns true when ANY descendant contains a yield, including inside a nested def, so it reports isGenerator=true for a function that merely RETURNS a generator. CPython disagrees with the oracle here: inspect.isgeneratorfunction is False for concurrent.futures._base.Executor.map, asyncio.coroutines.coroutine and ctypes.macholib.dyld.dyld_image_suffix_search, all three of which the oracle marks as generators. The parser stops at nested def/class boundaries and reports false, matching CPython. Note the helper has the same dead-code shape as `_declares` (a `continue` that does nothing, then a final unconditional ast.walk), so both may be worth a look. Parser unchanged; the differential checker now skips isGenerator for functions that contain a nested def, so real regressions are still caught elsewhere.
suggestedOracleFix: restrict _has_yield to the function's own body, and consider the same for _declares

note: All 10 frozen spine relations (262 columns) now emit. Byte-identical across runs for the full 10-relation output.

subject: receiverKind — the oracle's visit_Call ignores decorators entirely
detail: Two remaining sweep disagreements, both from the same root cause in the oracle's ast-side visit_Call: it computes `selfn = first_param_name if (first and self.cls)` and then tests `SELF if b.id == selfn else (CLS if b.id == 'cls' else NAME)`, which (a) never consults the decorator list and (b) string-matches the literal name 'cls'. Consequences: `@staticmethod def _interpolation_replace(match, parser)` calling `match.group(1)` is reported SELF (configparser.py:553,555) although a staticmethod has no receiver at all; and module-level `def __newobj__(cls, *args): return cls.__new__(cls, *args)` is reported CLS (copyreg.py:101,107) although it is a plain function parameter that merely happens to be named cls. The parser reports NAME for both, which is what the code says. Note the parser DOES report CLS for a genuine @classmethod, where the oracle reports SELF because its SELF test fires first — so the two disagree in both directions from one bug. Parser unchanged; differential checker exempts these shapes.
evidence: configparser.py:553,555 and copyreg.py:101,107 under the pinned 3.10.4
suggestedOracleFix: consult decorator_list before classifying the receiver, and drop the literal 'cls' string match

subject: keywordNames ordering and literal receivers
detail: Two more resolved in the parser's favour. (1) keywordNames: schema §2.16 c15 specifies SOURCE order; the oracle emits it alphabetically sorted. Source order is the contract and is also what argument flow needs. (2) A literal receiver such as "a,b".split(",") is reported UNKNOWN by the oracle; LITERAL is an explicit schema value (§2.16 c4) and strictly more informative. Both compared as sets / exempted in the checker rather than changed in the parser.

subject: six expression-stage drops found only by sweeping real code
detail: Each of these silently discarded facts and none was caught by the 18 fixtures. (1) A dict literal's children are `pair` nodes; dropping unrecognised nodes discarded every key and value in every dict, including calls — _strptime.py has six. Root cause was the design of the unknown-node path, so unrecognised nodes are now TRANSPARENT rather than dropped: worst case is a flatter tree, never a missing fact. (2) `d[a, b, c]` has three `subscript` field children and childForFieldName returns only the first, losing every index after the first (dataclasses.py:1081-1084). (3) An f-string inside an IMPLICIT concatenation — `f'{type(x)}' 'more text'` — parses to concatenated_string, which was treated as a literal leaf, so its interpolations and their calls vanished; common in error-message construction. (4) A sole generator-expression argument has NO argument_list wrapper, so its element and for-clauses were counted as separate positional arguments and calls inside the clause were lost. (5) `comment` is a named node and can sit between arguments, inflating positionalArgCount on commented multi-line calls. (6) Lambda parameter defaults are evaluated in the enclosing scope and were not walked at all (`lambda x=Nasty(): None`). Also fixed: expressionKindOf was enqueueing work AND returning null, so the transparent fallback re-enqueued the same node and every annotation sub-expression was emitted twice with an identical PK — classification is now documented as pure.

subject: A2 findings in manifest-native.jsonl
detail: Read all four open findings. typeCategory_classification (line 22, high, A3+A0) is mine and is accepted — the metaclass=ABCMeta / metaclass=EnumMeta idiom is currently misclassified because classifyType only inspects positional bases, not keyword arguments. Fixing next. The other three are A0's: comprehension_pairing (critical, oracle mis-pairs same-line nested comprehensions), parenthesized_list_splat and union_type (both unfixturable in the pinned grammar). I have not touched the oracle or staging fixtures, per boundaries. Will flip status by appending a resolution row referencing the same construct rather than editing A2's rows.

Accepted and fixed exactly as diagnosed. classifyType() now inspects the metaclass= keyword value with the same equality tests it applies to positional bases: metaclass=ABCMeta (and the dotted abc.ABCMeta) yields ABC_TYPE, metaclass=EnumMeta/EnumType yields ENUM_CLASS_TYPE. typeModifiersOf() now filters keyword bases the same way classifyType does and checks the metaclass explicitly, so the two passes can no longer disagree about whether a keyword entry counts — that disagreement was the root cause of the internally inconsistent typeModifier=ABSTRACT + typeCategory=CLASS_TYPE row. All 7 of A2's repro cases now match hand-derived expectations, including the two contrast cases that were already correct.
oracleGapAddressed: A2 is right that neither gate can see this field, so the fix is guarded by a direct assertion test rather than a differential one: src/test/python-scratch/classify-test.ts asserts typeCategory and the ABSTRACT modifier per class AND asserts the internal-consistency invariant that ABSTRACT never coexists with CLASS_TYPE. This is a self-check, not an oracle check — recorded as such. A0 still needs to surface ast.ClassDef.keywords as a metaclass field if these columns are to be oracle-adjudicated.

subject: typeCategory and typeModifier have no oracle coverage at all
detail: Seconding A2's oracle_gap note with a scope question. py_type.typeCategory (c3), typeAccess (c4), typeModifier (c5), typePlacement (c6) and mroKind (c21) are all ast-derivable and therefore Gate-2 territory by the schema's own layer-2 definition, but emit_oracle.py emits none of them and diff-decl compares only endLine and positional baseCount. The same is true of py_method.methodKind/methodModifier and py_import.importKind. These are currently guarded only by my own assertion tests, which share an author with the code under test and so detect regressions but not wrong premises. Worth deciding whether A0 extends the ast dump to cover them, or whether they are accepted as parser-adjudicated with self-tests as the only net.

Reproduced A2's finding from the parser side and confirmed the oracle is wrong, with independent evidence. For `result = [q for q in [r for r in z]]` the oracle attributes binding `r` to the scope at column 9 and `q` to the scope at column 21 — exactly swapped. CPython's own ast settles it: the ListComp at col 9 is `[q for q in [r for r in z]]` and binds q, the ListComp at col 21 is `[r for r in z]` and binds r. The parser emits col 9 -> q, col 21 -> r, i.e. correctly. Mechanism agrees with A2's root_cause: the outer comprehension's outermost iterable is evaluated in the ENCLOSING scope, so the inner comprehension is a SIBLING of the outer one and symtable constructs it FIRST; _pair_children's leftmost-column tie-break then pairs that first symtable child with the leftmost ast node, which is the outer comprehension.
gate1Exposure: Any file with same-line nested comprehensions will produce SPURIOUS Gate-1 binding disagreements, and the failure points at the parser. Confirming for the record that the parser must NOT be changed to match the oracle here. Not hit by my sweeps: the 250-file all-gates sweep and the 10,769-file scope sweep were Gate-1 clean, so the shape is rare in the stdlib — but it is silent when it occurs, which is the dangerous part.
evidence: src/test/python-scratch/nested-comp.py; ast.get_source_segment + generator targets under the pinned 3.10.4
action: no parser change; awaiting A0 fix to _pair_children

subject: Gate 1 across the full local corpus: 10,769 files
detail: Ran the scope/binding differential over every .py in the pinned CPython 3.10.4 stdlib and site-packages. Result: 10,757 files fully clean, 206,344 of 206,354 scopes and 1,449,036 of 1,449,064 bindings matching symtable exactly. Of the 11 files with any disagreement, ALL 11 are the same-line comprehension pairing defect A2 reported (construct comprehension_pairing) — every one is a scopeOrdinal swap plus the binding sets swapping with it. One further file (numpy executor.py) could not be judged because the oracle itself failed to produce output; the test harness now records that as unjudged rather than dying on it. Net: no known parser-side Gate-1 defect remains on this corpus.
corpusEvidence: Confirmed on real stdlib code, not just a synthetic repro: numpy/distutils/system_info.py:951 is `return [b for b in [a.strip() for a in libs.split(',')] if b]`. ast reports col 15 binds b and col 27 binds a; the parser emits exactly that; the oracle reports them swapped. Same signature as the earlier synthetic case.
action: no parser change; blocked on A0 fixing _pair_children

subject: grammar EXTRAS were counted as call arguments
detail: Line-continuation backslashes and comments inside an argument list are NAMED nodes in tree-sitter, so counting named children inflated positionalArgCount. Both occur in real code — ftplib.py:975 and idlelib/debugger_r.py:362 use a continuation inside the argument list, argparse uses inline comments. Fixed by testing tree-sitter's own `node.isExtra` rather than maintaining a blacklist of node types, and applied at every enqueue site so an extra can never become a phantom expression either. Found by the 1,500-file all-gates sweep; the 18 fixtures do not contain a continuation inside an argument list, which is a genuine fixture gap if A2 wants one.

subject: Full-corpus validation, all three gates: 13,586 files
detail: Ran the complete suite over every .py in the pinned CPython 3.10.4 stdlib and site-packages. 13,480 of 13,586 files fully clean (99.2%). Emitted 310,143 scopes, 2,087,179 bindings, 36,238 types, 276,798 methods, 467,124 parameters, 143,178 imports, 11,018,569 expressions and 1,337,938 call sites. 8 files could not be judged because CPython itself failed to produce ground truth; those are reported separately and never counted as passes. Every remaining disagreement falls into three classes, two of which are oracle-side and one of which is now fixed.

subject: grammar extras were counted as PARAMETERS as well as arguments
detail: Same root cause as the argument-list fix, in a place I had not covered: a comment or line continuation inside a PARAMETER list is a named node, so it was counted as a keyword-only parameter and inflated kwOnlyCount. Real occurrences: aiohttp/web_app.py:105 and web_protocol.py:162 both end a parameter with `debug: Any = ...,  # mypy doesn't support ellipsis`. Fixed by testing isExtra in every parameter iteration across all three extractors, including the receiver-detection path, so a comment before the first parameter cannot make a method look receiver-less. aiohttp is now 45/45 clean on all gates.

subject: CPython 3.10 reports FICTIONAL positions inside multi-line f-strings
detail: Resolved in the parser's favour with direct evidence. On the pinned 3.10.4, ast gives f-string interpolation sub-expressions positions that do not correspond to the source — this is the pre-PEP-701 f-string limitation. Minimal repro: for a line whose actual text is `    Thread: {threading.current_thread().name}`, where `threading` begins at column 13, ast reports the call at col_offset 36. The parser reports 13, the real position. Consequence: the ~14 remaining Gate-3 MISSING/SPURIOUS pairs are the SAME call reported at two different columns, not a missing fact. Keeping real positions is the right call because startColumn is in the py_expression primary key and a span must contain its own text; adopting ast's number would give spans that point at nothing. Real case: idlelib/run.py:415.
evidence: ast under the pinned 3.10.4 vs the source line

detail: Every remaining Gate-1 disagreement in the 13,586-file run is this one defect — there are no others. Two additions to A2's report. (1) It also affects nested LAMBDAS, not just comprehensions: py3_test_grammar.py:364 is `l4 = lambda x = lambda y = lambda z=1 : z : y() : x()`, three lambdas on one line all named `lambda`, where the leftmost-column tie-break cannot match construction order by construction. (2) Further real cases: py3_test_grammar.py:875 `(x for x in (y for y in a))` and :880, and test_generator_nested.py:105 `[Yield([e] + p) for p in perms([x for x in l if x != e])]`. Frequency: 11 files out of 13,586, so rare but silent.
action: no parser change; blocked on A0

subject: Gate 3 (runtime) — closing the no-oracle gap on typeCategory / typeModifier / methodKind
detail: Built a THIRD adjudicator for the fields no static oracle covers, because a self-test written by the code's own author catches regressions but cannot falsify a wrong premise. It imports the module and interrogates the LIVE OBJECTS with CPython introspection — dataclasses.is_dataclass, inspect.isabstract, inspect.iscoroutinefunction, inspect.isgeneratorfunction, __slots__, __dataclass_params__.frozen, _is_protocol, _is_runtime_protocol. That is different evidence in kind: the runtime knows what a class IS without reading how it was written, so a premise shared between the parser and a static checker cannot hide. Tooling: src/test/python-runtime/probe_runtime.py plus src/test/python-runtime-adjudicator.ts. Result on 366 stdlib modules: 1,307 classes and 436 methods checked, 26 disagreements found, 22 fixed, 4 residual and attributable. LIMITATION, stated plainly: importing executes module-level code, so 34 of 400 files could not be imported and are reported UNJUDGED, never as passes. This is a sampling check, not a corpus-wide gate.
residual: 4 of 1307. Two are cross-module bases (`class BrokenProcessPool(_base.BrokenExecutor)`) which are layer-4 engine work by §0.5. Two are a base bound by assignment to a call result (`_Instruction = collections.namedtuple(...)` then `class Instruction(_Instruction)`), which is constructor-call inference and belongs to the deferred py_type_inference relation. Neither is a defect; both are the documented layer boundary.

subject: typeCategory=CLASS_TYPE emitted alongside an ABSTRACT modifier on real stdlib code
detail: The self-contradictory row A2 predicted was still being produced — my own consistency assertion never fired because it only ever ran on my 7-class fixture, where the shape could not occur. The runtime adjudicator found it on the first real module containing ABCs: numbers.Complex, Real, Rational and Integral each emitted typeCategory=CLASS_TYPE with modifier=ABSTRACT,SLOTS. Cause: those classes inherit ABCMeta through a base rather than naming it, so only the @abstractmethod scan fired, and that scan set the modifier without touching the category. Fixed: a class declaring abstract members in its own body is ABC_TYPE. Purely syntactic — the decorators are in the class body — so no cross-module knowledge is needed. This is the concrete case for why a self-test is not a substitute for an independent authority.

subject: Python's THREE implicit method conversions were not modelled
detail: Python converts three dunders with no decorator written: __new__ becomes a staticmethod, and __init_subclass__ and __class_getitem__ become classmethods. The parser reported __class_getitem__ as DUNDER_METHOD where the runtime reports CLASS_METHOD (found on dataclasses.InitVar). This matters for the same reason a missed @classmethod does: it changes what argument 0 is, and therefore shifts every positional argument→parameter link. Now modelled, with __new__ keeping the more specific ALLOCATOR the schema designates for it.

subject: ABC_TYPE is NOT inherited by subclasses — caught mid-fix
detail: While adding same-module base propagation for typeCategory I initially treated ABC_TYPE as inheritable. The runtime adjudicator immediately rejected that: `class closing(AbstractContextManager)` descends from an ABC and is perfectly concrete, and inspect.isabstract agrees, so nine concrete contextlib classes were mislabelled ABC_TYPE. Abstractness depends on whether abstract methods remain UNIMPLEMENTED, which is per-class. PROTOCOL_TYPE and DATACLASS_TYPE are excluded from inheritance for the same kind of reason: subclassing a Protocol yields an implementation, and @dataclass decorates one class. Worth recording because the adjudicator caught both the original under-claim and my over-correction within the same session — which is the argument for having it.

subject: my own fixture asserted behaviour for code that cannot run
detail: A2's typeCategory repro included `class FunctionalEnum(metaclass=EnumMeta): RED = 1`, which I copied into a self-test. It raises TypeError at import — the Enum machinery needs its own base — so the assertion was about impossible code. Found immediately by trying to import the fixture. Frequency evidence on the underlying rule: across the 13,586-file corpus, metaclass=ABCMeta appears 219 times (A2's ABCMeta half is well justified and runtime-confirmed), while metaclass=EnumMeta/EnumType appears 3 times, of which the only one relying on the metaclass ALONE is the definition of enum.Enum itself — where the rule is correct. Rule kept; fixture corrected to the memberless form, which is what actually occurs.

subject: lambdas were not emitted as py_method at all
detail: Schema §2.7 lists `lambda` alongside `def` and `async def`, names it `<lambda>`, and justifies startColumn's place in the py_method PK entirely by lambdas (`g = (lambda: 1, lambda: 2)` gives two rows identical in name, qualifiedName, signature and startLine). Measured at 369 rows in A0's corpus. They were missing entirely, and three things broke silently as a result: (1) a LAMBDA scope's ownerHash had no py_method to point at, so it was falling back to the enclosing method and — at module level — to the py_module hash, giving a discriminator that says LAMBDA against a hash in the wrong relation; (2) every call inside a lambda body was attributed to the enclosing function, which is a real call-graph error since a lambda is a separately-invocable callable; (3) methodKind=LAMBDA and expressionOwnerKind=LAMBDA were never emitted. Now emitted in a dedicated pass, because lambdas are EXPRESSIONS and the statement walk never reaches those in defaults, decorators, class bases or comprehensions. Verified: `sorted(items, key=lambda item: compute(item.rank))` now attributes `sorted` to the enclosing function and `compute` to the lambda. +55 method rows over 400 stdlib files.

subject: invariant #1 was checking FK non-emptiness, not FK TARGET relation
detail: Appendix B #1 says a polymorphic FK resolves in the relation selected by its discriminator. My check only asserted non-emptiness, so a py_scope with ownerKind=LAMBDA pointing at a py_module PK passed: present, and non-dangling against the union of all PKs. Strengthened to resolve each discriminator against its own relation, and it immediately found a SECOND instance of the same bug — module-level comprehension scopes also pointing at the py_module hash instead of the enclosing method. Both fixed. Recording because the weak version of this check is worse than none: it reads as coverage while permitting exactly the error it names.

subject: decorator coverage — what IS and is NOT emitted
detail: py_decorator is one of the eleven DEFERRED relations, so it is deliberately not emitted, and with it go the decorator's own identity, its arguments, applicationOrder, replacesTarget and builtinKind. What IS captured, because it changes DISPATCH and therefore belongs on the spine: py_method.methodKind distinguishes PROPERTY_GETTER / PROPERTY_SETTER / PROPERTY_DELETER / STATIC_METHOD / CLASS_METHOD / ABSTRACT_METHOD / OVERLOAD_STUB, py_method.methodModifier carries PROPERTY|SETTER|DELETER|STATIC|CLASS|ABSTRACT|OVERLOAD|FINAL|CACHED, decoratorCount is recorded, py_type picks up DATACLASS_TYPE and the FROZEN / FINAL / RUNTIME_CHECKABLE modifiers, and every decorator EXPRESSION is emitted as py_expression with rootContext=DECORATOR and edgeRole=DECORATOR_EXPR, including a py_call_site with callKind=DECORATOR_CALL for a parameterised decorator such as @functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None). Verified on a probe covering all of these. The gap to state plainly: an @overload stub and its implementation are correctly distinguished as separate py_method rows, but nothing records that a decorator REPLACES the object it decorates — that is replacesTarget on the deferred py_decorator, so for now the engine must not assume a decorated name still refers to the def.
